sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report documents unauthorized transactional activity identified on account C10434-K1 belonging to customer C10434. Between 2016-12-02 and 2016-12-02, the financial institution detected an abnormal transaction burst comprising 1 unauthorized transaction(s) (including ID(s) 3506725). Total fraudulent exposure identified across the flagged activity amounts to $1,000.03 USD. All suspicious transactions were conducted through the electronic online payment channel, bypassing physical card-present point-of-sale security controls. Digital identity telemetry reveals that the unauthorized orders originated from a digital device signature (Windows | Windows 10 | edge 16.0 | 1366x768) that had never previously interacted with the cardholder's legitimate account. Further technical inspection confirmed that network traffic routed through an evasive proxy configuration designed to obfuscate the perpetrator's physical geography. A graph traversal analysis linked the identical device fingerprint to suspicious transactions on at least 25 other cardholder accounts, including C06958-K1, C07745-K1, C00854-K1, C04108-K1. When contacted by fraud operations, the legitimate cardholder formally repudiated the charges and confirmed the card remained in their continuous physical possession. The deliberate velocity, amounts, and digital fingerprints strongly indicate compromise of card numbers and credentials consistent with card not present new device. In accordance with institutional fraud policy and FinCEN guidelines, the compromised card was immediately blocked from further authorization, and connected accounts were placed under heightened continuous surveillance.

stop_reason: Customer denial settled the verdict; card compromised and protected.
